claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me begin with a basic question:

**How many children are you claiming Child Benefit for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit for my child. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your circumstances better.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old - he was born in 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That helps - Alex is currently 8 years old.

Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for clarifying that. Now let me check a few more important details about your circumstances.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming you're in the UK. However, I need to clarify a specific point about your immigration status, as this affects eligibility.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK (such as indefinite leave to remain)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Now, let me check one more important detail:

**Are you currently working, or what is your employment status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working, yes. Why do you ask?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good question! I ask because there are income thresholds that can affect Child Benefit eligibility. Specifically, if you or your partner earn above a certain threshold, it can impact your entitlement.

**What is your approximate annual income (or your household income if you have a partner)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. Well, I'm not sure of the exact figure off the top of my head, but I work full-time. What's the threshold you're talking about?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's a fair question. Let me first check the official guidance on Child Benefit eligibility to give you the accurate thresholds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've checked the official guidance, and I can see that the basic eligibility criteria don't mention a general income threshold for Child Benefit. However, there is a High Income Child Benefit Charge that applies if your income exceeds a certain level.

To give you accurate information, let me ask:

**Do you have a partner or spouse living with you, and if so, are they also working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just me and Alex at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now, to complete my assessment, I need to know about your income level.

**Approximately what is your annual income from your work?** (This will help determine if the High Income Child Benefit Charge applies to you.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd say I earn around £35,000 a year, roughly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful.

Before I provide my final assessment, let me just confirm one more thing:

**Are there any other circumstances I should be aware of regarding Alex - for example, is he in full-time education, does he have any special needs, or is there anything else about his situation I should know?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old, so yes, he's in primary school - full-time education. Nothing else unusual about his situation, just a normal kid!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Let me provide my final assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the necessary criteria:
- You're a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex lives with you and you're responsible for him
- Alex is 8 years old, which is under the age limit of 16
- Your income of around £35,000 per year is below the threshold where restrictions would apply
- Alex is in full-time education, which is normal for his age

You should be able to proceed with your claim. If you need to apply, you can do so through HMRC's official channels. Good luck with your application!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) You are responsible for Alex as he lives with you; (2) Alex is 8 years old, which is under 16, so he falls within the standard age range for Child Benefit eligibility; (3) You are a British citizen living in the UK, meeting the residency and citizenship requirements; (4) Your annual income of approximately £35,000 is below the threshold at which the High Income Child Benefit Charge would apply (which starts at £50,000 for a single claimant), so you are not subject to any income-related restrictions; (5) Alex is in full-time primary school education, which is normal for his age and does not affect eligibility.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. You should be able to proceed with your claim."
